elements.element: Customer is not bound by any employee non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause binds “neither party” and expressly states that the restriction “binds each party equally,” so Customer remains subject to a non-solicitation covenant.

elements.element: The non-solicitation restriction is mutual and binds both parties equally.
elements.evidence: The clause applies to “neither party” and expressly states that it is mutual and binds each party equally.

elements.element: The restriction applies only to personnel directly involved in the services.
elements.evidence: It covers only a person who was an employee of the other party and “was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.”

elements.element: The restriction lasts 12 months from the end of each covered person's involvement in the services.
elements.evidence: The operative restriction applies “[f]or a period of 12 months after the end of any person's involvement.” Read with the covered-person limitation, this ties the period to the end of that person's services involvement.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that the restriction “does not apply to general advertisements.”

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches by covered personnel are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that the restriction does not apply “to unsolicited approaches by any such person.”

elements.element: The clause does not prohibit hiring covered personnel.
elements.evidence: The original prohibition on hiring was deleted. The rendered clause prohibits solicitation only and contains no no-hire restriction.

result.reason: The operative language does not achieve the preferred position because Customer remains bound. It fully achieves the fallback: the covenant is mutual, solicitation-only, limited to directly involved personnel, runs for 12 months from the end of individual involvement, and includes both required carve-outs. The changes are substantively limited to implementing that fallback and do not disturb unrelated commercial terms. Drafting quality is reduced slightly by the redundant mutuality sentence and the mildly awkward phrase “after the end of any person's involvement,” though the intended trigger remains sufficiently clear in context.
